entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Siddharth Datt- Advocate for the appellant.

Shri A.N. Gupta- Government Advocate for the responden
Shri Vikas Jyotishi- Advocate for the objector.
Heard on I.A. No.17958/2025 , 3rd application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant.
Appellant's first and second applications were dismissed on merits vide order dated 26.09.2017 and 05.07.2024 respectively.

2. This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 25.01.2017 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Nagod, District Satna (M.P.) in S.T. No.55/2015, whereby the present appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction U/s. Imprisonment Fine In lieu of default 376 (2)Jha of IPC and 5(d) r/w 6 of Life Additional R.I. for 2 Rs.20000/-
POCSO Act imprisonment years With the direction that all sentences shall run concurrently 3.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Nagod, District Satna (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the present appellant.
It is further submitted that there are material contradictions and omissions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses.

The appellant has already undergone about 11 years of incarceration, therefore, in the light of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh Vs. The 2 CRA-685-2017 State of Uttar Pradesh [SLP (Cri.)
No.4633/2021], the application may be considered on the ground of period of incarceration.

sentences.text: This appeal is of the year 2017 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

4 . Learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the objector on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6 . Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh (supra) as well as the period of incarceration already undergone by the appellant, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant can be considered.
7. Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I.A. No.17958/2025 is allowed.

8 . It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 16.12.2025 and on such other dates, as 3 CRA-685-2017 may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
9. List the matter for final hearing in due course.

(VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (AJAY KUMAR   JUDGE JUDG  AL Khatti @ Salikram Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102481888/
